educationalGoal: The focus of this course is on the further development of all four language skills (speaking, listening, reading, and writing). This course also emphasizes authenti c learning. In this course, you will review grammar that you have learned at your school, and learn more vocabulary and communication skills that you will need for everyday life in Japan. You will also be made familiar with various aspects of Ja panese culture including sociolinguistic facts about accurate communication.
advice: Most of the time, this course is conducted in Japanese, and students are expected to use only Japanese during th e class. Required Materials Handouts that you will receive in class. Moodle Site The Japanese Communication 2 has a Moodle course management site (https://e-learn01.mars.kanazawa-it.ac.jp/). Al l information about course related materials, such as assignments, will be posted on this site. It is your respo nsibility to check the site regularly to keep track of what is going on in the course.

    評価の要点   評価方法 行動目標 評価の実施方法と注意点     試験 ① レ There will be two tests, during which understanding of grammar structures, listening comprehen sion, and speaking skills will be assessed.   ② レ   ③ レ   ④ レ   ⑤ レ   ⑥     クイズ
小テスト ① レ Daily review quizzes will assess your understanding of grammar structures, kanji, vocabulary, and culturally appropriate usage. Quizzes are usually given at the beginning of class. Make-up quizzes will be allowed only with written documentation of a legitimate reason for the absenc e.   ② レ   ③ レ   ④ レ   ⑤ レ   ⑥     レポート ① レ You will take turns presenting a kanji you have found in real-life contexts, such as signs, me nus, or instructions. You should take a photo of the kanji in use and present its meaning, rea ding(s), and an example of how it is used. This activity helps build practical kanji knowledge and encourages students to engage with the language in their daily environment. Kanji introdu ced may be included in review quizzes.   ②     ③ レ   ④ レ   ⑤ レ   ⑥     成果発表
(口頭・実技) ① レ You will give a short in-class speech (approximately 1 minute). The speech should be based on a personal experience, such as a recent event, cultural observation, travel experience, or dai ly life in Japan. This activity is designed to improve spoken fluency, build confidence, and e ncourage cultural exchange. You are expected to prepare in advance and speak without reading a full script.   ② レ
